k1.author: curator-D
k1.quote: svc.apply(app) submits an application. Application fields: id, age, income, employment (employed or self_employed), requested_limit.
k1.text: Call svc.apply(app) with the application dict (fields: id, age, income, employment (employed or self_employed), requested_limit). The request shape is unchanged in API v2; only the response shape changed. (source: spec)

k2.author: curator-D
k2.quote: svc.apply now returns {"api_version": 2, "result": {"outcome": "approved" | "declined" | "manual_review", "credit_limit": <int>}}. The v1 fields `decision` and `limit` are removed.
k2.text: Calloway is now on API v2 (current). svc.apply returns {"api_version": 2, "result": {"outcome": "approved" | "declined" | "manual_review", "credit_limit": <int>}}. The v1 fields `decision` and `limit` are removed. The v1 shape (decision "approve"/"decline"/"refer" and integer limit) is deprecated.

k2b.author: curator-D
k2b.quote: svc.apply returns a dict with `decision` ("approve", "decline" or "refer") and `limit` (an integer, 0 unless approved).
k2b.text: In API v1 (deprecated), the response had `decision` ("approve", "decline" or "refer") and `limit` (an integer, 0 unless approved). Calloway is now on API v2 where these fields are removed.

k3.author: curator-D
k3.quote: outcome manual_review replaces refer and is handled as in spec section 3.
k3.text: handle(app, svc) returns {action, limit}. Map the partner outcome to an action: approved -> issue with the returned credit_limit; declined -> decline with limit 0; manual_review -> queue_review with limit 0 (do not decline). In API v2, outcome "manual_review" replaces v1 "refer" and is handled exactly as spec section 3 prescribes.

k3b.author: curator-D
k3b.quote: approve: issue the card with the returned limit. decline: decline the application. refer: the application is not decided; place it in the manual review queue (action queue_review) and do not decline it.
k3b.text: API v2 outcome->action mapping: "approved" -> action "issue" with the returned credit_limit; "declined" -> action "decline" with limit 0; "manual_review" -> action "queue_review" with limit 0 (do not decline it).

k4.author: curator-D
k4.quote: For every partner in the network, whatever the partner decided, an application from a self_employed applicant whose requested_limit is above 4000 must be placed in manual review (queue_review) instead of being issued. A decline stays a decline.
k4.text: Network referral rule: for any partner, a self_employed applicant whose requested_limit is above 4000 must be placed in manual review (queue_review) instead of being issued, regardless of the partner's decision. A decline stays a decline.

k5.author: curator-D
k5.quote: an application from a self_employed applicant whose requested_limit is above 4000 must be placed in manual review (queue_review) instead of being issued.
k5.text: The network referral rule applies only to self_employed applicants (not to all partners/applicants); an employed applicant is not forced into review by requested_limit.

k6.author: curator-D
k6.quote: an application from a self_employed applicant whose requested_limit is above 4000 must be placed in manual review (queue_review) instead of being issued.
k6.text: The referral threshold is strictly "above 4000" (requested_limit > 4000); a self_employed applicant with requested_limit exactly 4000 is not forced into manual review by the network rule.
